newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CSFB Russia equities head quits.
newsitem.headline: CSFB Russia equities head quits.

text.p: CS First Boston Russian equities head Peter Halloran is leaving the firm to start up an investment fund and will be replaced by a CSFB team at the Moscow office, CSFB said on Tuesday.

Halloran, 35, who led a sales team that generated over $5 billion in turnover in the first half of the year, up from a few billion in the last half of 1996, will open Moscow-based equity fund Pharos Capital.

Pharos Capital Management Limited said in a statement it intended to raise $150 million in a month's time and Halloran said it would focus on shares but could invest up to 25 percent of funds each in direct investment and fixed income.

The new CSFB Moscow equities management team will include four people, CSFB global head of European equities sales Martin Newson said from London, adding the team would take over in a transition period over the next one to three weeks.

Senior trader Igor Rozhkov in Moscow will be promoted to Head of Russian Equity Trading. London-based Western European equity trader Garry Jensen will be rebased in Moscow to become Head of Russian Sales and Sales Trading.
Senior Russian analysts Stuart Amor and Andre Arofikin will continue to divide their time between London and Russia and will also be on the management team.

Halloran, who joined CSFB in 1991, was extremely important to the CSFB operation, generating $8 billion in fixed income sales last year and $1.6 billion in arranged corporate finance commitments in addition to equity sales, company sources said.
Another member of the Russian equity team is also leaving the company for Pharos, company sources said.
Newson said the new management team would be a fitting replacement for Halloran, despite his value to CSFB. "Overall, we are probably strengthening the business somewhat."
CSFB, part of Credit Suisse, is one of the oldest Western players in Russia and is considered to be one of the largest traders on the market.
A group of executives led by Boris Jordan left CSFB in 1995 to set up Renaissance Capital, which recently merged with Bank MFK (ICFI), part of the MFK-Uneximbank group.
